# RV power station and solar combo

I only have a direct store link for one product, the ALLPOWERS R4000. For the others, the links go to the review pages that list them, not to a store. Check current prices and bundles on the brand's own store or Amazon.

## First, size it to your RV
A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup, so a small unit won't start it ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). If you won't run the AC off battery, a 1,000-2,000 Wh unit is enough for a fridge, lights, a laptop and Starlink.

## My picks

**1. Best for a big RV or running the AC: ALLPOWERS R4000 (3,456 Wh, 3,600 W)**
- It has an RV outlet and takes up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs (650 W each, 12-60 V). It uses LiFePO4 and has a 5-year warranty.
- The store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 took it to about $1,319.12 in a cart test on 2026-10-23. It expires 2026-11-15, and checkout has the final word.
- Caveats: it weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it is a place-it-and-leave-it unit. You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. The [product page](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) has the details.

**2. Name-brand alternative: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, 4,000 W)**
- [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) rates it the best all-round RV station for 2026. EcoFlow is also known for the fastest recharging ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)).
- It costs more than the ALLPOWERS, and I don't have a current price for it.

**3. Best mid-size and budget: BLUETTI AC200L (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W)**
- It accepts up to 1,200 W of solar and has a built-in 30A RV outlet. It weighs about 62 lb ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) recommends it for budget shoppers.

**4. Best for weekends and light loads: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 or EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (about 1,000 Wh)**
- These suit a fridge, device charging and a Starlink Mini. The Jackery accepts only 400 W of solar, while the DELTA 3 Plus accepts 1,000 W ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Solar panels
None of my sources named specific panels for these units, so I won't recommend a model. Match the array to the station's solar input limit, since a bigger array than the unit accepts is wasted. For the R4000, that means up to three 650 W strings within 12-60 V. For the AC200L, the limit is 1,200 W. For a roof-mounted RV array, check the unit's voltage range before buying panels.

If you tell me your RV size, whether you want to run the AC, and your budget, I can narrow this to one combo.
